title: The Smallest of Three
statement: Three numbers are drawn independently and uniformly from $[0,1]$. What is the expected value of the smallest one?
insight: Three random points cut the interval into four gaps that are exchangeable, so each has expected length 1/4.
hints: The smallest value is the length of a particular gap.
Three points split $[0,1]$ into four pieces. Is any piece special?
Think of 4 points on a circle of circumference 1, one of which is the cut.
solution: Place 4 uniform points on a circle of circumference 1 and cut at one of them. The other three are uniform on $[0,1]$, and the four arcs between consecutive points are exchangeable by symmetry. The arcs sum to 1, so each has mean $\tfrac14$. The first gap is the minimum: $E[\min] = \tfrac14$, and in general $\tfrac1{n+1}$.
